newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota develops emission-free fuel cell car.
newsitem.headline: Toyota develops emission-free fuel cell car.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp, Japan's biggest car maker, said on Friday that it had developed an electric car powered by a fuel cell that produces no toxic emissions.
The environmentally friendly car runs on electricity generated by a reaction between hydrogen and oxygen in the fuel cell and the only by-product is water vapour, Toyota said.
A company spokeswoman said the new car, based on Toyota's recreational vehicle the RAV4L V, was a prototype and it was not clear when it might hit the market.

Germany's Daimler-Benz unveiled the world's first fuel cell-powered car in May, saying the technology represented the industry's most realistic hope for eventually mass-producing a practical, pollution-free vehicle.
Automakers are working on various ways of cutting pollution from cars to meet emissions standards and appeal to environmentally conscious customers.
Japan's Mitsubishi Motors has launched a gasoline direct injection engine in Japan that it says produces considerably less carbon dioxide than standard engines.

The energy conversion efficiency of the Toyota fuel cell system is more than 60 percent, two to three times that of gasoline engines, Toyota said. The only by-product of the fuel cell system is clean water vapour, it said.
Toyota currently markets another type of electric car powered by nickel-metal hydride batteries that sells for 4.95 million yen ($44,500).
The Toyota spokeswoman said the fuel-cell car would be commercially viable if the company could produce and sell it for around the same price.
Fuel cells were originally developed to power space craft. ($1=111 yen)
